processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast lightweight steel (fully austenitic cast steel) of nominal composition Fe-30Mn-9Al-XSi-0.9C-0.5Mo.
Calcium treatment with argon stirring was used as the melt practice for the 1.56% Si, 0.002% P heat, improving cleanliness/ductility.
Solution treated at 1050°C for 2 h followed by water quench to produce a fully austenitic matrix.

structures.overall_structure: Fully austenitic matrix (solution-treated condition); no spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering in the austenite.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Percent elongation measured in a 25.4-mm (1-in.) gage length; hardness Brinell (3000 kg) converted from Rockwell B and C scale measurements.
Dynamic fracture toughness (J_Id) determined by the Schindler single-specimen technique using instrumented Charpy impact tests on fatigue precracked specimens.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: dynamic fracture toughness (DFT): 700 kJ/m2 (1.56% Si, solution treated) vs 94–136 kJ/m2 (Cast 4130 quenched and tempered)

characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm whether spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering occurred in the solution-treated austenite.
characterization_methods.key_findings: No spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering within the austenite in solution-treated specimens, regardless of Si content.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai F20 scanning/transmission electron microscope
characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm whether spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering occurred in the solution-treated austenite.
characterization_methods.key_findings: No spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering within the austenite in solution-treated specimens, regardless of Si content.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Ab initio calculations were combined with experimental results (XRD, TEM, APT) to explain the Si–C interaction.

analytical_models.model_name: Si–C repulsive interaction / carbon activity in austenite
analytical_models.equation_role: Explains increased carbon partitioning into κ-carbide and stabilization of κ-carbide with Si addition.

parameters.name: carbon partitioning coefficient in κ-carbide (1.56% Si steel, aged 60 h at 530°C)
predicted yield strength increase (spinodal hardening mechanism)

analytical_models.model_note: Silicon partitions to austenite during aging and decreases the austenite lattice parameter; the repulsive Si–C interaction forces increased carbon content in κ-carbide. In solution-treated specimens, no spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering occurred.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemistry of the 1.56% Si, 0.002% P heat (Table I, wt%): Si 1.56, C 0.89, Mn 29.97, P 0.002, S 0.007, Mo 0.53, Al 8.81, Cu 0.006.
In the solution-treated condition, cast steels have high work-hardening rates (with elongations up to 64%).
Silicon additions in the range 0.59–1.56% Si have no significant effect on the mechanical properties of solution-treated steels (but increase tensile strength and hardness during aging).

Inclusion analysis (Fig. 15): total inclusion density for the three low-phosphorus silicon-containing steels (0.59%, 1.07%, 1.56% Si) was similar at 62–78 inclusions/mm2; porosity in the 0.59% Si steel was almost double that of the 1.56% Si steel.
